title: Dependency Chorus Conductor and Visibility Bridge
creator: Leah Martinez
description: Create a lightweight, repeatable protocol and dashboard (the 'Chorus Conductor' + 'Visibility Bridge') that maps initiative-level dependencies across Engineering, Design, Security, and Infra so PMs can predict blockers, align OKR milestones, and automate onramp actions for upcoming cycles. The output is a runbook + data-backed dashboard that surfaces dependency health, ownership, mitigation status, and recommended play actions for the next 2 cycles.
acceptance_criteria: Dependency model defined with 5 canonical dependency types (API contract, infra capacity, security review, design handoff, data availability)
Dashboards populate automatically from the dependency intake board and GitHub PR status for at least 2 pilot initiatives
Playbook documents mapping from signal -> recommended action (escalate, schedule canary, sandbox, fallthrough) with owners assigned
Automated weekly readiness score generated per initiative that correlates with cycle commit likelihood
Pilot completed with two cross-functional initiatives and < 1 week average triage time for new blockers

Instrument intake form in Linear with new fields (type, owner, due-by, blocking-for) — ENG: implement by 2025-03-10 (ENG-1842)
Prototype dashboard in Metabase/Looker using intake + GitHub status — Data: create views by 2025-03-12
Run two pilot reviews with Eng/Design/Security/Infra for Q2 initiatives — schedule weeks of 2025-03-17 and 2025-03-24
Finalize runbook and emergency escalation playbook — publish Confluence page by 2025-04-01
Post-mortem template and cadence for dependency misses — define and include in runbook
notes: Motivation: PMs currently spend ~30% of pre-cycle planning time chasing owners and clarifying blocker scope; recurring late discoveries cause sprint churn.
We want a signal-first approach: combine explicit intake metadata with passive signals (PRs, infra quota errors, security ticket state) to auto-surface risk.
Design constraints: keep process light for 1-2 engineer/pm minutes per dependency — avoid heavy gating that slows delivery.
Trade-offs considered: stricter gating increases predictability but reduces velocity. We'll trial advisory controls first with escalation lanes before gating.
Pilot scope excludes compliance-heavy private deployments until security team signs off on the data model for risk classification.
decisions: Adopt 5 canonical dependency types to reduce taxonomy ambiguity (API contract, infra capacity, security review, design handoff, data availability) — agreed 2025-02-28
Visibility Bridge will be read-only for infra/security leads initially; editing rights are reserved for owning teams to avoid incorrect state changes — agreed 2025-03-04
Start with advisory readiness scores (0-100) computed weekly, not blocking CI; gating will be re-evaluated after 2 cycles — agreed 2025-03-06
links: GitHub PR for intake form automation: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1245
risks: Low adoption if the dashboard requires manual updates — mitigation: automate using PR and ticket signals
Taxonomy mismatch between teams — mitigation: two-week alignment workshops and a single source-of-truth in Confluence
Signal noise leading to false positives on readiness score — mitigation: tune thresholds during pilot and expose signal provenance in UI
Sensitive security signals in dashboard may need redaction for external partners — mitigation: role-based views planned post-pilot
